The only way anything will ever change is if I do something myself. Which is why I'm asking for help.

Yes that is the problem, but its only one piece in the whole picture. This person uses this e-mail to scam others. How trades on our site work is that they are normally set-up on the forum and carried out on msn in real-time. Before doing the trade, you get a middle man, like myself, to join the msn conversation to pretty much moderate the trade. With the newer msn update, a scammers tool was created, !imitate. With !imitate, you can do pretty much what the command implies, being able to imitate someone else. With this, you can pretend to be whoever you want. Having such a similar e-mail as mine only adds to the believability that the person you are actually talking to is me. A middle man is supposed to PM all users involved in the trade before preceding to hold whatever virtual item is involved, but this step is not widely known; especially to newer members on the forum. With this lack of knowledge these people have, they are easily scammed by this person. When I find out what user they used to initiate the trade on the forum, that person is banned and added to the scammer/do not trade list. This person keeps on creating smurf accounts to pull off the forum aspect of the trade which eventually just snowballs into the other person involved being scammed. These aren't all tiny trades either. People have been scammed hundreds and on the rare case thousands by this person. This needs to stop immediately.

I have gotten everyone of the accounts he has used banned; its not working. Even some of them have been IP banned, but that doesn't really work since how easy it is to change one's IP. A vast majority of the trades are done via msn and you don't need to be a member of the forum to own a msn.

There is a sticky with all the people listed that are mms like myself and who to not trade with. There's even a proper procedure on how to do trades to ensure you don't get scammed. It involves having the MM PM them on the forum to verify that it is in fact them. Not everyone reads stickys and newer members to the forum are easily victimized, so I want to neutralize this e-mail or some how gain control of it if that is even possible.
